cards.title: Stochastic Simulation and Estimation (SSE) for Design Evaluation
cards.claim: Stochastic Simulation and Estimation (SSE) is a valuable method for evaluating the efficiency of sparse sampling designs. By simulating multiple datasets (e.g., 1000 replicates) from a known 'true' model and fitting them with candidate models, one can quantify the probability (power) of correctly identifying the true model structure under different sampling constraints.
conditions: Requires a well-characterized 'true' model from prior rich data.
Computational intensity: requires fitting thousands of datasets.
Model selection criteria must be predefined (e.g., ΔOFV > 3.84 for 1 df).
required_inputs: Final population PK model parameters and variability estimates.
Software capable of automated simulation and fitting (e.g., NONMEM with PsN SSE script).
limitations: Results are dependent on the accuracy of the 'true' model used for simulation.
Does not account for all real-world data collection errors or protocol deviations.
cards.downstream_use: Prospective evaluation of sampling strategies before conducting a new study to minimize resource use while maintaining model identifiability.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
